paras: The Watertown posse pursuit of a Black barber was a manhunt in Watertown, apparently in Dakota Territory, reported in February 1882, in which a citizens' posse pursued an unnamed Black barber accused of attempting to rape a local woman. The single report said that he would be dealt with summarily if caught, but it gave no outcome, and no later report was found.

The episode is known from one paragraph in the "Dakota News" column of the Jamestown Alert of 17 February 1882, a digest of territorial items that ran alongside Washington dispatches on Dakota statehood dated 11 February. The paragraph gave no date for the incident and named neither the barber nor Mrs. Merrill's first name.

According to the column, "a negro barber" broke into the residence of Mrs. Merrill of Watertown and attempted to rape her. Her cries brought help, and the accused man fled. A "posse of citizens" then went after him, and the item said that if caught he would be "dealt with in a summary [manner]."
No report of the man's capture, arrest, trial or death appears in the coverage, and the size and membership of the posse were not given.

The Jamestown Alert ran the story as one sentence-pair among unrelated territorial news, between a note on a Yankton murder suspect's release and speculation about the territorial marshal's office. It stated the accusation as fact, identified the man only as "a negro barber" and "the negro," and reported the posse's intention of summary punishment without comment. No other paper carrying the item was found.
